explanation: Tenth Circuit panel expressly overruled Robison on the State's need to cross-appeal a procedural-bar ruling, but states it submitted the determination to the entire en banc court, which agreed; full-court approval is a recognised ground, so limb 3 fails.

Waco court expressly overruled its own National Loan Investors on which judicial-estoppel law applies, giving no panel-exception ground; but from my knowledge the Waco court had only three justices, so Gray, Vance and Reyna were the whole court, not a panel.

Eastland Court of Civil Appeals overruled a contrary indication in its own Wagstaff, relying on the earlier Supreme Court-approved Adams decision; from my knowledge 1939 civil appeals courts were three-justice courts sitting as a whole with no en banc procedure, so limbs 2-4 fail.

Corpus Christi court overruled Nunez and its other De Garmo sufficiency-waiver decisions, but did so in an opinion expressly issued en banc under Tex.R.App.P. 49.7 after withdrawing the panel opinion; the bench limb fails.

San Antonio court expressly overruled Seiler's holding that filing a condemnation petition in the wrong place is jurisdictional, but the judges line lists seven justices sitting, which from my knowledge is the full court sitting en banc; the bench limb fails.

Federal Circuit panel overruled the TTAB's British Seagull decision as contrary to 37 C.F.R. 2.122(b), not its own Brunswick opinion; footnote says Brunswick affirmed only on functionality and never reached the evidentiary issue, so no same-court holding was departed from.

Alabama Court of Criminal Appeals overruled Beshears so far as guns alone were treated as exigent circumstances, but 'All the Judges concur' except one; from my knowledge that five-judge court sits as a whole, with no panel or prior-panel rule.
